A reference of questions about documents

Source: R/doc-bench-qa.R
gr_qa_reference.Rd

Builds an hr_reference() whose items are questions about documents, for benchmarking reading recipes with gr_arm() and scoring them with gr_scorer_answer().

Usage

gr_qa_reference(
  questions,
  documents,
  answers,
  split,
  cluster = documents,
  unanswerable = NULL
)

Arguments

questions

The questions, a character vector. Its names, when every question has one, are the item ids; otherwise the ids are q1, q2, and so on, zero-padded to a common width so they sort in order (q01 to q10 for ten questions).

documents

The document each question is about: a character vector of file paths, web addresses or text (one per question, or one for all), or a list whose elements may also be chunks from gr_segment().

answers

The acceptable answers, one element per question: a character vector with one answer each, or a list whose elements are character vectors of alternatives. NA or an empty element for a question with no answer (an unanswerable one, or one not yet labelled). Numbers are taken as text.

split

The split of each item, one per item or one for all; see hr_reference(). When split is not given, every item goes in "dev".

cluster

The cluster of each item, one per item or one for all. By default, the document.

unanswerable

Which questions the document does not answer: NULL for none, a logical vector (one per question, or one for all), item ids, or positions.

Value

An hr_reference().

Details

Each item's payload, what an arm is given, is a list of question and document. Its label is the list of acceptable answers, any one of which an answer must contain to be right. An unanswerable item, one the document does not answer, is labelled "NOT_IN_DOCUMENT": the reader is right when it says the document does not hold the answer. That an item is unanswerable is held in its label alone, so an arm cannot read it from the payload. An answer given as "NOT_IN_DOCUMENT" marks its item unanswerable too. An item that is neither unanswerable nor given an answer has no label, and every run on it is scored NA.

Items are clustered by document by default, since questions about one document share its errors: a document given as a path or address is its own cluster name, and text or chunks are named by a hash of their content.

See also

gr_arm(), gr_scorer_answer(), hr_benchmark()

Other harness: gr_arm(), gr_scorer_answer(), hr_arm(), hr_benchmark(), hr_contrast(), hr_drift_check(), hr_mdd(), hr_reference(), hr_report(), hr_scorer()

Examples

ref <- gr_qa_reference(
  questions = c(revenue = "What was revenue in 2024?",
                units = "How many units did Sheffield produce?",
                ceo = "Who is the chief executive?"),
  documents = gr_example(),
  answers = list(c("45.2 million", "45,200,000"), "12,400", NA),
  unanswerable = "ceo", split = "test")
ref
#> <hr_reference> 3 item(s) in 1 cluster(s)
#>   splits: test 3 
#>   hash: 5a83551bcb88
ref$labels$ceo
#> [1] "NOT_IN_DOCUMENT"
